CUB.hook: The largest island in the Caribbean and the longest — end to end it covers about the distance from London to Edinburgh, yet sits only 145km from Florida.
CUB.place: The long island guarding the mouth of the Gulf of Mexico, directly south of Florida.

HTI.hook: The only nation founded by a successful slave revolt, in 1804 — and the first independent country in Latin America.
HTI.place: The western third of Hispaniola, sharing one island with the Dominican Republic.

DOM.hook: Holds the highest peak in the entire Caribbean, Pico Duarte at 3,101m — high enough that it occasionally gets frost.
DOM.place: The eastern two-thirds of Hispaniola, the island between Cuba and Puerto Rico.

JAM.hook: Its Blue Mountains are steep and wet enough that the coffee grown there sells for several times the world price.
JAM.place: South of Cuba and west of Hispaniola, on its own in the middle of the sea.

BHS.hook: Around 700 islands, only about 30 of them inhabited — and the seabed beside the shallow banks drops away to 4,000m.
BHS.place: The long scatter northeast of Cuba, beginning just off the Florida coast.

TTO.hook: Home to Pitch Lake, the largest natural asphalt deposit on Earth — parts of London and New York are paved with it.
TTO.place: Just 11km off Venezuela's northeast tip, the last stop at the bottom of the island arc.

BRB.hook: Sits out in the Atlantic beyond the island arc rather than in it, which is why hurricanes so often pass it by.
BRB.place: Alone to the east of the chain, past Saint Vincent — the most easterly country in the Caribbean.

LCA.hook: The Pitons rise straight out of the sea as twin volcanic spires — the only place in the Caribbean with a drive-in volcano.
LCA.place: Midway down the eastern arc, between Martinique and Saint Vincent.

VCT.hook: One main island plus 32 smaller ones, and a volcano — La Soufrière — that erupted as recently as 2021.
VCT.place: In the eastern arc, directly between Saint Lucia and Grenada.

GRD.hook: The Isle of Spice, and one of the world's great nutmeg producers — the nut is on the national flag.
GRD.place: The southern end of the eastern arc, just north of Trinidad.

DMA.hook: The Nature Island, with the world's second-largest boiling lake — and no relation whatsoever to the Dominican Republic, 800km northwest.
DMA.place: In the eastern arc between Guadeloupe and Martinique. The mix-up with the Dominican Republic is the one to watch for.

ATG.hook: Claims a beach for every day of the year — 365 of them, one for each day.
ATG.place: Near the top of the eastern arc, east of Saint Kitts.

KNA.hook: The smallest sovereign state in the Americas by both area and population — the whole country would fit inside Liverpool.
KNA.place: Near the top of the eastern arc, northwest of Antigua.
